gloss: to get new; to replace with new

definitions.gloss: getting something new, having something newly made
definitions.explanation: The act of acquiring a new item, especially clothing, furniture, or equipment, often to replace something old or worn out. Implies purchasing or having something custom-made.

examples.japanese: スーツを{新調|しんちょう}する。
{入学式|にゅうがくしき}に{合|あ}わせて{靴|くつ}を{新調|しんちょう}した。
examples.english: I got new shoes in time for the entrance ceremony.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}くなったカーテンを{新調|しんちょう}しようと{思|おも}って、いくつかの{店|みせ}を{見|み}て{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: I went around several stores, thinking about getting new curtains to replace the old ones.

notes:
USAGE:
{新調|しんちょう}する implies purposefully acquiring something new, often with a sense of replacing something old or preparing for an occasion. It is most commonly used for clothing, accessories, and household items.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スーツを{新調|しんちょう}する: to get a new suit
- {着物|きもの}を{新調|しんちょう}する: to get a new kimono
- {家具|かぐ}を{新調|しんちょう}する: to get new furniture
- {制服|せいふく}を{新調|しんちょう}する: to get a new uniform

NOTE:
Unlike simply "buying" ({買|か}う), {新調|しんちょう}する carries the nuance of replacing something or preparing something fresh for an occasion. It can also imply having something custom-made rather than buying off the shelf.
